newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate firms to 7.9 from 7.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate firms to 7.9 from 7.6 pct.

text.p: The Croatian lending rate firmed to 7.9 percent on Friday from 7.6 percent, boosted by demand for fresh loans made at higher rates.
Total Money Market settlements rose to 18.3 million kuna from 11.5 million, against 110 million on offer. Delears said new loans accounted for 16.3 million.
Interbank call money and insurers' five-10 day rate were steady at eight and seven percent, respectively.
The 10-15 day rate was higher at 10 percent, up from seven two days ago, but volume was low.
Thursday's overnight trade totalled 38.8 million kuna, leaving a surplus of 325.5 million kuna after three banks with shortfalls squared their positions.

The central bank said it stayed out of foreign exchange market on Friday. Its kuna midrate for Saturday and next Monday eased to 5.2805 against the dollar and to 3.5576 versus the mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
